content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To meet an eagle, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Print out high-resolution maps of the nature reserve (10 minutes)
Step 2. Research eagle nesting patterns online (2 hours)
Step 3. Purchase a heavy-duty waterproof jacket (1 hour)
Step 4. Pack a specialized bird-watching field kit (30 minutes)
Step 5. Charge the batteries for the long-range walkie-talkies (4 hours)
Step 6. Check the local mountain weather forecast (5 minutes)
Step 7. Buy a physical compass at the sporting goods store (20 minutes)
Step 8. Fill the SUV with a full tank of premium gas (10 minutes)
Step 9. Apply waterproof spray to your hiking boots (15 minutes)
Step 10. Withdraw emergency cash from the ATM (5 minutes)
Step 11. Secure the eagle-watching permit to your backpack (2 minutes)
Step 12. Call the park ranger station for trail conditions (10 minutes)
Step 13. Load the cooler with sandwiches and water (20 minutes)
Step 14. Download an offline GPS navigation app (15 minutes)
Step 15. Clean the lenses on your spotting scope (10 minutes)
Step 16. Double-check the first aid kit for bandages (5 minutes)
Step 17. Read a book on eagle behavioral biology (6 hours)
Step 18. Pack a pair of thermal gloves (5 minutes)
Step 19. Set the alarm clock for sunrise (2 minutes)
Step 20. Borrow a high-quality tripod from a friend (1 day)
Step 21. Wash your mud-caked hiking boots (30 minutes)
Step 22. Inspect the tread on your mountain tires (15 minutes)
Step 23. Pack a lightweight portable camping chair (5 minutes)
Step 24. Verify the dates for the eagle migration season (30 minutes)
Step 25. Calibrate the focus on the digital camera (15 minutes)
Step 26. Attend an introductory ornithology seminar (3 hours)
Step 27. Sharpen your pocket knife (10 minutes)
Step 28. Renew your annual national park pass (15 minutes)
Step 29. Pack a high-calorie trail mix (10 minutes)
Step 30. Purchase a professional-grade pair of binoculars (1 hour)
Step 31. Buy a sun hat with a neck flap (15 minutes)
Step 32. Organize your gear in the trunk of the car (30 minutes)
Step 33. Watch a documentary on golden eagles (90 minutes)
Step 34. Check the local sunrise and sunset times (5 minutes)
Step 35. Buy a detailed topographic trail map (20 minutes)
Step 36. Print out the driving directions to the trailhead (5 minutes)
Step 37. Request a vacation day from work (1 day)
Step 38. Buy a notebook for logging bird sightings (10 minutes)
Step 39. Prepare a thermos of hot coffee (15 minutes)
Step 40. Buy a durable weather-resistant backpack (45 minutes)
Step 41. Research the specific eagle species in the area (1 hour)
Step 42. Drive from your home to the nature reserve entrance (3 hours)
Step 43. Buy a portable power bank for your phone (30 minutes)
Step 44. Clean the tripod mounting plate (5 minutes)
Step 45. Put on your hiking layers and boots (10 minutes)
Step 46. Lock the car and hide your valuables (5 minutes)
Step 47. Adjust the straps on your camera harness (5 minutes)
Step 48. Subscribe to a bird-sighting alert newsletter (10 minutes)
Step 49. Study the specific trail markers on the park website (45 minutes)
Step 50. Test the emergency whistle on your bag (1 minute)
Step 51. Pack a lightweight rain poncho (5 minutes)
Step 52. Apply a thick layer of sunscreen (5 minutes)
Step 53. Sign the visitor log at the trailhead (2 minutes)
Step 54. Pick up a printed trail brochure at the gate (5 minutes)
Step 55. Check the battery level on your smartphone (1 minute)
Step 56. Update your emergency contact information (5 minutes)
Step 57. Set your watch to the correct local time (1 minute)
Step 58. Hike to the designated observation cliff (2 hours)
Step 59. Drive to the trailhead parking lot (20 minutes)
Step 60. Clean the dust off your binoculars (5 minutes)
